theory.target: For the frozen dimension-24 cubic auxiliary function, characterize the exact admissible cutoff set and certify outward dyadic cutoff/objective rounding; distinguish invalid downward/nearest rounding from a valid improvement of the prior cutoff 15.
definitions: P(u)=225+13u+13u^2-u^3 and Q(u)=(u-15)^2(u+1), u=pi*|x|^2, n=24; both origins equal 225.
A positive real cutoff T is admissible exactly when every real u>=T has P(u)<=0.
Alpha denotes the unique positive root of P; equality at the tail endpoint is allowed.
B(T)=T^12/(4^12*12!) is the covered-volume bound from this fixed function, conditional on the published packing theorem.
Dyadic precision b ranges from 1 through 32; the upward endpoint is the least k/2^b strictly above alpha, the downward endpoint is one step below.
The objective interval encloses the optimum for this fixed function only, and its lower endpoint is not a lower bound on packing density.
assumptions: Only the prior fixed cubic P and Q and dimension 24; no optimization over polynomial coefficients.
Cutoff T is a positive real number in u units, not Euclidean radius; f<=0 for all u>=T is required.
The density objective is B(T)=T^12/(4^12*12!), because P(0)=Q(0)=225; lower bounds on B for this fixed function are not packing-density lower bounds.
Exact rational arithmetic, no floating-point proof or assumed tolerance.
The source heading is unchanged and needs human scope review; no parent-solution, novelty, higher-degree or broader-dimensional claim.
approaches_considered: Retain the sufficient cutoff 15 and substitute a nearest-rounded numerical last root: the substitution is falsified by a positive endpoint.
Replace the sufficient grid restriction by an algebraic admissibility characterization, exact sign bisection and upward cutoff/objective propagation.
Independently reconstruct root isolation with generic Sturm variations and Fourier transforms with radial differentiation.
falsification_targets: Nearest rounding of a root preserves a global tail inequality.
Opposite endpoint signs alone establish uniqueness of a positive root.
A lower endpoint for the fixed-function objective is a packing-density lower bound.

claims.statement: For the fixed cubic P, the admissible real cutoffs are exactly [alpha,infinity), where alpha is its unique positive root in (14,15). B(alpha) is optimal only for this fixed auxiliary function. Ordinary proof given; not independently authored/kernel accepted.
claims.falsification_condition: An extra positive root, failure of positivity below alpha, or a gap in monotonicity/endpoint reasoning.

claims.statement: Rounding the final positive root to the nearest dyadic cutoff always preserves the required tail sign.
claims.falsification_condition: At three bits nearest T=119/8 has P(T)=1793/512>0.

claims.statement: The 32-bit interval (63944510808/4294967296,63944510809/4294967296) contains the unique positive root. Its upper endpoint U gives exact B(U)=U^12/(4^12*12!), with ratio to the previous B(15) below 183/200.
claims.falsification_condition: A different root count, nonnegative P(U), incorrect Fourier pair or objective, or failed exact ratio comparison.

claims.statement: Both algorithms agree on all 32 directed-rounding rows; all lower cutoffs and 15 nearest cutoffs fail. Seven altered certificates are rejected.
claims.falsification_condition: A table mismatch, omitted bit depth or accepted invalid control.

claims.statement: Cohn--Elkies v3 Theorem 3.2 uses equal positive origins and non-strict sign conditions; its center-density bound needs the unit-ball factor for covered volume.
claims.falsification_condition: Incorrect version, locator, normalization or theorem assumptions.
